issues_detected.description: version_access.latest_version_doi is 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42', an identifier that appears nowhere else in the record: versions_available lists 3.1.0 as doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66 (which is also the record's own id and doi) and 3.0.0 as doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68. A reader cannot tell whether 37yb-1t42 is a PhysioNet project-level 'latest' DOI, an unlisted newer version, or a transcription error, and the record offers no source_caveat for it while caveating far smaller discrepancies elsewhere.
issues_detected.recommendation: Either identify 10.13026/37yb-1t42 explicitly (e.g. as the version-independent PhysioNet project DOI) in version_details, or set latest_version_doi to doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66 to match the newest version enumerated.

issues_detected.description: regulatory_restrictions asserts hipaa_compliant: compliant and other_compliance states 'HIPAA de-identification rules were applied', while the same block's source_caveats records that the Data Transfer and Use Agreement characterizes the transferred data as personally identifiable information under OMB M-07-16 and states it is 'not covered under HIPAA, FERPA, or similar laws'. The record explicitly declines to reconcile these, leaving the compliance claim logically unsettled even though the underlying deidentification method (HIPAA Safe Harbor) is described in detail.
issues_detected.recommendation: Scope the HIPAA statement to the released registered-access feature set (where Safe Harbor was applied) and note separately that the raw-audio DTUA governs data the provider treats as PII outside HIPAA; this resolves the tension without discarding either source.

issues_detected.description: data_protection_impacts records that 'no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted', yet sensitive_elements declares race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, psychiatric diagnoses and biometric voice, and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states that k-anonymization with k>=2 is not achieved. The absence of any impact assessment is a substantive governance gap for this data profile, faithfully reported but not mitigated by any documented compensating analysis.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record whether the ethics module's sensitive-field review and the controlled-access memorandum constitute a de facto impact analysis, or state that a DPIA-equivalent assessment is planned, with scope and owner.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false and confidential_elements_present is false, while participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states that 'K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved for the released tables' and that voice 'cannot be fully de-identified'. The two are reconcilable (raw waveforms are withheld; the flags describe the released feature tables), but the boolean reads more absolutely than the risk narrative supports.
issues_detected.recommendation: Qualify identifiable_elements_present with a note that it refers to direct identifiers in the registered-access release only, and that residual re-identification risk from quasi-identifier combinations is not eliminated.

issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes gives only '12 months' of collection, sourced from healthsheet documentation written against an earlier release, while the release history in distribution_dates runs from version 1.0 (November 2024) through 3.1.0 (May 2026) and version 3.0.0 alone added 391 participants. A 12-month window is difficult to square with a cohort of 833 accrued across five sites and six releases under an award running 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30. The record flags the caveat itself but supplies no start or end date.
issues_detected.recommendation: State calendar start and end dates for collection behind version 3.1.0, or state explicitly that collection is ongoing and that the 12-month figure describes only the initial accrual period.

issues_detected.description: Three award identifiers are recorded for one grant without resolution: PhysioNet's '3OT2OD032720-01S1', RePORTER application '3OT2OD032720-01S3' under core project 'OT2OD032720', and two corrupted documentation footer strings ('3Tf-OTOD03272001S2', '3TF-OT2ActfOD032720Projectf01S1'). All non-corrupted forms match NIH conventions (OT2 activity code, OD institute, six-digit serial, -01S<n> supplement suffix), so the formats validate, but a machine consumer cannot determine which supplement funded this release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Designate the PhysioNet-acknowledged supplement as the dataset's funding award and retain the RePORTER application number as a cross-reference, marking the two footer strings as transcription artifacts rather than candidate identifiers.

issues_detected.description: keywords contains only four terms ('health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice'), which does not reflect the eighteen diagnostic categories enumerated in the phenotype file_collection (Parkinson's disease, ALS, laryngeal cancer, COPD and asthma, PTSD, bipolar disorder and others) or the modality terms carried in the description. Discoverability by condition depends on prose inside a collection description rather than on indexed terms.
issues_detected.recommendation: Extend keywords with condition and modality terms (e.g. dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, depression, spectrogram, speech biomarker) and, where possible, bind them to SNOMED CT or ICD-10 codes already used for labeling.

issues_detected.description: conforms_to_schema names the D4D metadata schema (https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema) rather than any data-level standard, and source_caveats correctly declines to assert BIDS v1.9.0 conformance for 3.1.0 because the PhysioNet layout is features/metadata/phenotype rather than the documented b2ai-voice-audio BIDS layout. The restraint is well-reasoned, but it leaves the release with no asserted data standard, which limits harmonization with other voice corpora.
issues_detected.recommendation: State whether the features/metadata/phenotype layout derives from BIDS, and if a data dictionary convention (e.g. JSON sidecars per file stem) is followed deliberately, name it as the applicable standard.

issues_detected.description: No total_size_bytes, file_collections.total_bytes or total_file_count is given. Per-feature record counts (32,522 torchaudio pitch down to 28,640 sparc EMA) and 833 participants permit an order-of-magnitude estimate only; a user cannot plan storage or transfer for dense Parquet tensors of dimension 201xT.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record byte sizes per file_collection and a total file count for the 3.1.0 release.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 uses the PhysioNet registrant prefix (10.13026) and is consistent with publisher https://physionet.org/ and page https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/, whose version segment matches the version field '3.1.0'.
RRID:SCR_007345 in the citation matches the RRID:SCR_ pattern and is the correct resource identifier for PhysioNet as the hosting platform.

Grant OT2OD032720 parses correctly as an NIH Other Transaction award (OT2 activity code, OD as the Office of the Director, six-digit serial), which is the expected mechanism for a Common Fund Bridge2AI data generation project.

The issued date 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z agrees exactly with the distribution_dates entry 'Version 3.1.0: 1 May 2026', and the related_datasets is_new_version_of target 10.13026/k81f-qr68 agrees with the versions_available entry for 3.0.0 dated 16 December 2025 — temporal ordering across collection, versioning and publication is internally coherent.

The deidentification method is appropriate to the data type and unusually well matched to it: HIPAA Safe Harbor for tabular phenotype data, plus withholding of all raw waveforms precisely because voice is itself a biometric identifier, plus exclusion of spectrograms and MFCCs derived from free speech. The privacy design follows the risk rather than a generic template.

Preprocessing is described at parameter level (16 kHz mono with Butterworth anti-aliasing; 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT; 60 Mel bins; sparc at 50 Hz; ppgs at 100 Hz over 40 phoneme categories), which makes the feature tables reproducible from raw audio by a third party holding controlled access.

Differing per-feature record counts are explained rather than left as an anomaly: representations derived from sensitive records and audio checks were withheld and some files could not generate certain features, and the record declines to compute a single recording total that no source states.

known_biases uses BiasTypeEnum values (selection_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias) and the measurement_bias entry identifies a real confound — cohorts recruited at different sites on distinct iPad devices, confounding diagnostic label with recording apparatus — which is the kind of finding an AI/ML user needs before modeling.

Access tiers are cleanly separated and each is actionable: registered access on PhysioNet for credentialed users signing the Registered Access Agreement for features, versus DACO review, Data Access Request Form, DUA and institutional DTUA for raw audio served from Synapse syn72370534.

External resource URLs (github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, github.com/sensein/senselab, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724, isca-archive.org, synapse.org) are all structurally well-formed and point to domains consistent with the roles claimed for them; Zenodo prefix 10.5281 and ISCA prefix 10.21437 are correct registrars.

The record repeatedly marks provenance conflicts with source_caveats rather than silently choosing (author name spellings, Health Data Nexus versus PhysioNet maintenance answers, healthsheet answers written against v3.0.0, grant identifier variants), which raises confidence in the unqualified statements.

participant_id and session_id are declared as identifiers carried by every feature file and phenotype table, giving an explicit join key for integrating dense Parquet features with tabular phenotypes — the concrete integration capability Q10 asks for.

overall_score.denominator_note: normalized_percentage = 80 / 88 (adjusted) x 100; fixed_percentage = 80 / 88 (full rubric) x 100. No question was excluded, so the two bases coincide and excluded_item_ids is empty.

questions.name: Field Completeness
questions.description: Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated (id, title, description, keywords, license).
questions.score_label: ≥90% fields populated
questions.evidence: id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description ~1,300 chars; keywords: 4 terms; license_and_use_terms.license_terms with data_use_permission: general_research_use; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; creators: 16 entries with affiliations; purposes: 3 responses; instances: 2 entries (833 human participants; audio recordings by derived features); resources: 11 named resources nested under file_collections[features]; variables: 4 (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted. parent_datasets: absent.
questions.quality_note: Thirteen of the fourteen enumerated fields carry meaningful content (≈93%). Only parent_datasets is unpopulated, and its function is discharged elsewhere by related_datasets with a typed derives_from link to the raw-audio Synapse accession. resources appear nested inside file_collections rather than at top level, which is the schema-appropriate placement for per-file entries.
questions.semantic_analysis: Field population is not merely nominal: instances carry ontology terms (B2AI_TOPIC:25, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41), and confidentiality_level 'restricted' agrees semantically with a registered-access license plus a separate controlled-access tier for raw audio. The one weakness inside a populated field is variables, which describes the four Parquet element columns but not the hundreds of phenotype columns; those are instead covered by the per-file JSON data dictionaries described in file_collections, so the gap is documented rather than hidden.

questions.name: Entry Length Adequacy
questions.description: Whether narrative fields (description, purposes) have meaningful content length.
questions.score_label: >200 chars
questions.evidence: description is approximately 1,300 characters and names cohort size (833 adults), five North American sites, four disorder families plus controls, the tablet/headset protocol, and an itemized list of released feature types (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch and periodicity traces, SPARC articulatory estimates, phonetic posteriorgrams, openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth static features, audio quality metrics, per-recording metadata, phenotype tables). purposes holds three responses of roughly 180–260 characters each.
questions.quality_note: Far above the >200 character threshold, and the length is informative rather than padded: the description states explicitly that raw waveforms are not in this release, which is the single most consequential fact for a prospective user.
questions.semantic_analysis: Narrative content is semantically consistent with the structured fields it summarizes — the 833 figure matches instances.counts, the five-site claim matches sampling_strategies, and the enumerated feature types match the eleven resources under file_collections[features] one for one. No inflation or drift between prose and structure was detected.

questions.name: Keyword Diversity
questions.description: Number of unique keywords provided to describe dataset topic coverage.
questions.score_label: 3–7 keywords
questions.evidence: keywords: ['health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice'] — four unique terms.
questions.quality_note: Four keywords falls in the 3–7 band. The terms are apt but generic; none names a condition, a modality, a population or a feature type, so keyword-driven discovery will not surface this dataset for searches on dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, cough, depression or spectrogram features.
questions.semantic_analysis: Checked the rubric's permitted supplements: condition coverage exists (eighteen diagnosis phenotype files, from airway stenosis to unilateral vocal fold paralysis) and ontology references exist (B2AI_TOPIC:25, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41 on instances; ICD-10 named as the annotation protocol). These are real and they partly offset the thin keyword list, but they sit in prose inside a file_collections description and in instance-level annotations rather than in indexed terms, so they do not lift the count into the ≥8 band. Score held at the band floor with the supplement noted.

questions.name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
questions.description: Number of distribution formats and file type diversity.
questions.score_label: 2–3 file types
questions.evidence: distribution_formats: TSV (text/tab-separated-values), JSON (application/json), Parquet (media type deliberately omitted with a note that no IANA type is stated by the sources) — three formats. file_collections: three collections (features, phenotype, metadata) with eleven individually named resources under features, each with dimensions and record counts (e.g. torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet, 201 by T, 29,278 records; sparc_ema.parquet, T by 12, 28,640 records). total_file_count: absent.
questions.quality_note: Exactly three unique formats and three unique media types places this at the top of the 2–3 band rather than in the >3 band. The enumeration itself is excellent — eleven named files with shapes, parameters and per-file record counts, plus a stated JSON data dictionary for every data file — but the counting criterion for this question is format variety, and the dataset is deliberately narrow there.
questions.semantic_analysis: Format variety is semantically appropriate rather than deficient: dense time-series tensors in Parquet, scalar per-recording features in TSV, and machine-readable dictionaries in JSON is a coherent three-format design. The multimodality signalled in the description (acoustic, articulatory, phonetic, questionnaire) is achieved through content within these three containers and through participant_id/session_id joins, not through additional file types, so the modest score reflects the counting rule and not a documentation failure. No total_file_count is given, which is a small enumeration gap.

questions.name: Data File Size Availability
questions.description: Presence of file size or instance count metadata.
questions.score_label: Pass — numeric instance and record counts found
questions.evidence: instances[0].counts: 833 human participants. instances[1].notes gives per-feature record counts: torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and sparc pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc EMA 28,640. splits documents that no predefined train/validation/test splits exist. subpopulations documents cohort membership. total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes: absent.
questions.quality_note: Passes on instance and record counts, which are given at unusual granularity — per feature file rather than a single headline number. No byte sizes are given anywhere, so sizing a download remains an estimate.
questions.semantic_analysis: The record counts are internally consistent and their variation is explained by withheld sensitive derivations and generation failures, which is a stronger form of documentation than a single round total. Cross-checked 833 participants against subpopulations and the phenotype description (one row per participant per session, multiple sessions for a subset) with no contradiction.

questions.name: Dataset Identification Metadata
questions.description: Presence of unique identifiers such as DOI, RRID, or persistent URLs.
questions.score_label: Pass — multiple persistent identifiers plus hosting platform
questions.evidence: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; publisher: https://physionet.org/; citation carries RRID:SCR_007345; version_access lists per-version DOIs (doi:10.13026/249v-w155 for 1.1, doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68 for 3.0.0, doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84 for 1.0 on Health Data Nexus).
questions.quality_note: Passes comfortably: a version-specific DOI, a landing page, a named publisher and a platform RRID are all present, and prior versions carry their own DOIs.
questions.semantic_analysis: The 10.13026 prefix is PhysioNet's registrant prefix and is consistent with both publisher and page domain; 10.57764 is consistent with the Health Data Nexus attribution for version 1.0. RRID:SCR_007345 matches the RRID:SCR_ pattern. The one blemish, carried to Q13, is version_access.latest_version_doi (10.13026/37yb-1t42), which matches no version listed here.

questions.name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
questions.description: Presence of funding sources, grants, creator affiliations, and institutional sponsors.
questions.score_label: Funders with grants + creators with affiliations
questions.evidence: funders[0].grantor: 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, Bridge2AI Program' with two grants — 3OT2OD032720-01S1 (the PhysioNet acknowledgement, with the full project title quoted) and OT2OD032720 (the RePORTER core project, held at the University of South Florida, PI Yael Emilie Bensoussan, 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30, FY2025 award 4,660,942 USD). creators: 16 entries, each with an affiliation (USF Health Morsani College of Medicine, Weill Cornell Medicine, Vanderbilt University Medical Center, Hospital for Sick Children, Washington University in St. Louis, OHSU, Simon Fraser University, The Hastings Center, MIT, University of Toronto, Sinai Health, University of Florida), most with a role description; the consortium entry names a principal_investigator with email and department.
questions.quality_note: Both halves of the top band are satisfied and exceeded: grant numbers with period, amount and administering institution, and per-creator affiliations with module roles (data acquisition, tools and IT infrastructure, ethics, per-cohort leads).
questions.semantic_analysis: OT2OD032720 parses correctly against NIH conventions (OT2 activity code for Other Transaction awards, OD for Office of the Director, six-digit serial), and the -01S1 supplement suffix is well-formed. The award period and the Common Fund mechanism are consistent with a Bridge2AI data generation project, and purposes ('flagship dataset that enables future research in artificial intelligence') align with the funding programme's stated goals. The record flags, without reconciling, that RePORTER shows application -01S3 while PhysioNet acknowledges -01S1, and that the documentation footer strings are corrupted; that ambiguity is logged as a low-severity correctness issue but does not undercut the funding documentation itself.

questions.name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
questions.applicability_evidence: Human-subject involvement is evidenced by fields outside Q8: description states '833 adult participants recruited at five North American sites' who 'completed a standardized protocol of acoustic tasks' (Q1/Q2); keywords include 'health' (Q3); and collection_mechanisms describes 'A custom Bridge2AI-Voice application running on a tablet, with a head-mounted headset and microphone', with data_collectors recording that 'data was collected in the clinic with the assistance of a trained research assistant' (Q12).
questions.description: Comprehensive ethics coverage including IRB approval, deidentification, privacy protections, informed consent, participant compensation, and vulnerable population safeguards.
questions.score_label: Comprehensive human subjects protections documented
questions.evidence: ethical_reviews: USF IRB approval with the Single IRB arrangement and separate Canadian REB submissions. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, irb_approval, ethics_review_board, regulatory_compliance (HIPAA deidentification, Certificate of Confidentiality assertable against subpoenas, no DMC, not a drug/device study), special_populations (adults 18–120; cohorts include mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's and other dementias, mood and psychiatric diagnoses). is_deidentified: HIPAA Safe Harbor plus indirect-identifier removal, an itemized identifiers_removed list, and deidentification_details covering transcript review, removal of free-speech derivations and REDCap-flagged sensitive fields. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques, reidentification_risk (voice cannot be fully de-identified; k>=2 not achieved; contractual bar on contacting subjects), data_linkage. informed_consent: consent_obtained true, three consent modalities, five-year documentation retention, consent_scope covering registered versus controlled access and the absence of non-commercial or geographic restriction, withdrawal_mechanism. collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations describe the process and the post-collection irrevocability. participant_compensation: gift cards, 40 USD under 90 minutes, 80 USD over, capped at 120 USD. at_risk_populations: adult-only enrollment, assent options, discomfort risk in mood cohorts. data_protection_impacts: states that no impact analysis has been conducted.
questions.quality_note: Every protection area in the question is addressed, most with operational specifics a reader could act on (dollar amounts, retention periods, the named consent modalities, the exact assertion the Certificate of Confidentiality supports). The scoring band is met. The one substantive gap is that no data protection impact analysis exists; the record documents that absence plainly rather than papering over it, which is why the score is held at the top band with the gap recorded as an issue rather than scored as missing documentation.
questions.semantic_analysis: Cross-field logic passes on the human-subjects chain: involves_human_subjects true is matched by populated ethical_reviews and by informed_consent with a described process; is_deidentified is matched by a named method and by participant_privacy protections. The deidentification method is appropriate to the data type — Safe Harbor for tabular phenotypes is insufficient for voice, and the record recognizes exactly that by withholding all waveforms and excluding free-speech-derived spectrograms, which is a substantively correct rather than boilerplate response. Two tensions were flagged: identifiable_elements_present: false sits uneasily beside 'k of two or more is not achieved', and hipaa_compliant: compliant sits against the DTUA's own statement that the data is 'not covered under HIPAA'. Both are recorded in the datasheet's own caveats, which is why neither was treated as concealment.

questions.name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
questions.description: Whether access policy, license, IP restrictions, regulatory restrictions, and confidentiality level are clearly defined.
questions.score_label: License + restrictions + confidentiality classification
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms: Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License requiring signature of the Registered Access Agreement, credentialed PhysioNet user from version 3.0.0, no additional training; raw audio governed separately by Data Access Request Form, DUA, DACO review and an institutionally signed Data Use and Transfer Agreement; duplication for the research project permitted, sale prohibited, no fees; data_use_permission: general_research_use. ip_restrictions: four clauses (no transfer of IP; no IP claims that would block access to data or conclusions; downstream IP permitted subject to non-obstructive licensing and the Fort Lauderdale Agreement; no third-party IP restrictions on the instances). regulatory_restrictions: no export controls; confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; other_compliance covering safeguards, access restriction to authorized persons and five-business-day breach reporting. data_governance: DACO as committee, USF Board of Trustees as accountable organization, a two-tier access_review_process, five stewardship_roles, and DACO@b2ai-voice.org as the contact.
questions.quality_note: Exceeds the top band. Governance is not merely asserted but decomposed into roles, an application pathway per access tier, an accountable institution and a working contact address, with the reason an office rather than a named individual is given explained in a note.
questions.semantic_analysis: The governance package is plausible and internally proportionate: confidentiality_level 'restricted' matches a registered-access licence for features and a committee-reviewed tier for biometric audio, and the IP clauses are consistent with the prohibited_uses entry barring IP-based restrictions on access. The governance contact appears under data_governance rather than under regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact, which is a placement difference and not an omission. The unreconciled HIPAA/DTUA statement is the one logical tension; the record surfaces it explicitly rather than choosing silently, so the score is not reduced, and the issue is reported under semantic_analysis.issues_detected.

questions.name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
questions.applicability_evidence: The datasets-shared condition is met by fields outside Q10's own scoring emphasis: distribution_formats carries access_urls to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ (Q4/Q17), and license_and_use_terms permits use 'solely for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by Authorized Researchers' under a signed registered-access agreement (Q9/Q18).
questions.description: Presence of standard formats, ontologies, schema conformance, cross-platform dataset linkages with typed relationships, and dataset integration capability.
questions.score_label: Standard formats + partial schema/ontology compliance + documented integration capability
questions.evidence: distribution_formats: TSV, JSON and Apache Parquet, described as 'an open-source column-oriented data file format'. conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema with conforms_to_class: Dataset. Every data file is paired with a JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem, 'giving a description of each column, the question asked of the participant where applicable, and the data type of the response'. Integration keys: variables declares participant_id and session_id as identifiers 'carried by every feature file and phenotype table', and each Parquet element carries participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames. related_datasets: four typed relationships (is_new_version_of, derives_from, references, is_documented_by). external_resources: b2aiprep, senselab, the REDCap data dictionary with Zenodo archive, the documentation repository with Zenodo archive, and Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles. instances carry B2AI_TOPIC:25 and B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41. conforms_to (data-level standard): absent, with source_caveats explaining that BIDS v1.9.0 conformance is documented for the b2ai-voice-audio layout but not asserted for this release's features/metadata/phenotype layout.
questions.quality_note: Standard open formats, a declared metadata schema, column-level JSON dictionaries, ontology-coded instances, typed cross-dataset links and an explicit join key together sit close to the top band. Held at 4 because the release asserts no data-level standard: the datasheet reasons its way to that position honestly, but a consumer harmonizing this corpus with other voice datasets has no declared structural standard to target, and no compression metadata is given.
questions.semantic_analysis: conforms_to_schema names the datasheet's own LinkML metadata schema, not the data layout — a distinction the evaluation must keep, since crediting it as data standardization would overstate interoperability. Integration capability is genuine and testable rather than asserted: the same two identifiers are declared across both the dense Parquet features and the tabular phenotypes, which is precisely the cross-modality join Bridge2AI AI-readiness criteria look for. The FHIR profiles reference is a real semantic-interoperability asset but is listed without a locator, so it could not be weighed heavily.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.applicability_evidence: The software condition is met by external_resources (a Q14 field), which references code repositories: 'b2aiprep, the library used to organize and preprocess the dataset ... at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep' and 'SenseLab ... at https://github.com/sensein/senselab', plus https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap. extension_mechanism.contribution_url additionally points to https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep. Q11's own fields were not used to establish applicability.
questions.description: Mentions of preprocessing, cleaning, and labeling strategies with software tools used in data preparation, including annotation quality, imputation, and missing data documentation.
questions.score_label: Comprehensive strategies with software versions/URLs
questions.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: six entries with parameters — mono conversion and 16 kHz resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter; STFT spectrograms at 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, downsampled by two in time; Mel spectrograms with 60 bins and 60 MFCCs; SPARC articulatory kinematics and source features at 50 Hz; ppgs phonetic posteriorgrams at 100 Hz across 40 phoneme categories; openSMILE, Parselmouth and Praat static features; Whisper Large transcription. cleaning_strategies: a named audit protocol (missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, schema checks on categorical responses, per-task audio QC, silence and duration checks, produced-versus-intended speech comparison) executed with b2aiprep and SenseLab, plus released audio_quality_metrics.tsv. labeling_strategies: clinical gold standard with annotations_per_item: 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_protocol 'Per Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes', data_annotation_platform. machine_annotation_tools: nine tools with per-tool role descriptions and a tool_accuracy caveat that 'transcription, were generated using off-the-shelf models that have not been audited for correctness'. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling strategy. Version and locator evidence: 'b2aiprep ... version 3.0.0 generated this release', Whisper Large named, Apache-2.0 and MIT licences recorded for the repositories. imputation_protocols: absent.
questions.quality_note: Meets the top band. Strategies are comprehensive and given at parameter level, the generating library is named with its version and URL, and the labeling path is documented end to end including a single-annotator limitation and an explicit statement that transcription models were not accuracy-audited. Residual gaps are minor: no version pins for openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth, torchaudio, sparc or ppgs, and no imputation protocols — the latter consistent with a pipeline that documents missingness rather than filling it.
questions.semantic_analysis: Tool-to-output attribution is coherent throughout: each named tool maps onto specific released files (torchaudio to the four torchaudio Parquet files, sparc to the four sparc files, ppgs to ppgs.parquet, openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth to static_features.tsv), so the software claims are checkable against file_collections rather than free-floating. The tool_accuracy caveat is an unusual and credible admission for a dataset record. The absence of imputation_protocols is semantically appropriate here, not an omission, because missing_data_documentation states that missingness is reported in a missingness table rather than imputed; scoring treated it accordingly.

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.applicability_evidence: Both halves of the condition hold on fields outside Q12: datasets are shared (distribution_formats with PhysioNet access_urls and a research-permitting licence, Q9/Q17), and data collection is identified independently of Q12 by description ('Participants completed a standardized protocol of acoustic tasks on a tablet application') and by direct_collection.is_direct: true.
questions.description: Description completeness of data collection mechanisms, acquisition methods, data collectors, and collection timeframes.
questions.score_label: Full collection protocol with methods, collectors, and timeframes
questions.evidence: acquisition_methods: two entries with provenance flags — session-based recording and questionnaire administration with diagnoses confirmed against audio/imaging, EHR or prescriptions (was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects, was_validated_verified all true), and a second entry marking released features as was_inferred_derived. collection_mechanisms: the custom tablet application with named hardware (iPad 9th/10th generation and iPad Air 5th generation, Avid AE-36 microphone via an Apple dongle, distinct devices per site) and REDCap for questionnaire instruments. data_collectors: three roles (research team including students, clinicians listed as IRB co-investigators providing gold-standard diagnoses, hospital staff assisting logistics) with per-role detail. collection_timeframes: 12 months, with a caveat that no start or end dates are stated and that the figure comes from a healthsheet written against an earlier release. raw_data_sources: two entries (WAV audio via the tablet app; REDCap export) with access_details naming Synapse syn72370534 and DACO@b2ai-voice.org. Supporting: sampling_strategies (non-probability recruitment at high-volume expert clinics, screened against per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria), direct_collection, collection_consents, collection_notifications.
questions.quality_note: All three components named in the top band — methods, collectors and timeframes — are present, and the protocol extends well beyond them to recording hardware, per-site device assignment, screening, consent conduct and raw-source disposition. The timeframe is the weakest element: a duration without calendar bounds, self-flagged as possibly not covering collection behind 3.1.0.
questions.semantic_analysis: The protocol is internally consistent and explains a downstream finding: distinct iPads per site, recorded here, is the same fact that known_biases.measurement_bias identifies as confounding label with apparatus — the collection description and the bias analysis corroborate each other rather than merely coexisting. Temporal consistency could not be fully verified and is logged as a medium-severity issue: a 12-month window is hard to reconcile with six releases between November 2024 and May 2026 and with 391 participants added at version 3.0.0 alone. Because the field is populated, sourced and caveated, and every other component is complete, the score was not reduced below the band.

questions.name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
questions.applicability_evidence: Same condition as Q12: collection is identified outside Q13 (description, direct_collection, acquisition_methods) and the dataset is shared (distribution_formats access_urls, registered-access licence).
questions.description: Presence of version information, version access methods, errata, update plans, release notes with dates, and data sustainability indicators.
questions.score_label: Comprehensive versioning and sustainability documentation, with one unresolved version identifier
questions.evidence: version: '3.1.0'. version_access: latest_version_doi doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42; versions_available listing 1.1 (17 January 2025, doi:10.13026/249v-w155), 2.0.0, 2.0.1, 3.0.0 (doi:10.13026/k81f-qr68) and 3.1.0 (doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66); version_details stating that each version has a unique DOI, that older versions continue to be supported by default subject to the publishers' right to remove access, that version 1.1 files are no longer available, and that 1.0 was published on Health Data Nexus under doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84. errata: per-version corrections (2.0 reprocessed spectrograms and removed free-speech-derived spectrograms and MFCCs; 2.0.1 corrected authorship; 3.1.0 fixed broken Parquet files, back-filled validated diagnoses, rearranged phenotype files and renamed gold-standard variables), with a caveat that the documentation claims no erratum exists. updates: semi-annual release plan with notification channels, explicitly marked as a plan written against Health Data Nexus rather than an observed cadence, followed by the actual publication history. maintainers: PhysioNet/MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, NIH under OT2OD032720, and the consortium with the DACO contact. Sustainability also covered by retention_limit (indefinite for the published dataset; two years for raw-data recipients with certified destruction; ten years for identifiable linking sheets) and extension_mechanism.
questions.quality_note: Nearly everything the top band asks for is present: persistent identifiers per version, a domain-appropriate biomedical repository, a named long-term governance structure and institutional/funding commitment, plus genuine errata and a stated cadence. Reduced by one point for a version-identifier inconsistency inside this question's own fields — latest_version_doi names 10.13026/37yb-1t42, which matches none of the versions enumerated and is not the record's own 3.1.0 DOI, leaving the pointer to 'latest' unresolvable.
questions.semantic_analysis: The semantic issue drove the deduction and is recorded in issues_detected. Everything else cross-checks: the 3.0.0 DOI in versions_available matches the related_datasets is_new_version_of target, the 3.1.0 date matches both distribution_dates and issued, and the platform migration from Health Data Nexus (1.0) to PhysioNet (1.1 onward) is stated consistently in maintainers, version_details and distribution_dates. The update plan is correctly labelled a plan rather than reported as observed behaviour, which avoids a common overclaim. PhysioNet is a domain-appropriate repository for biomedical signal data, satisfying the sustainability criterion substantively and not just nominally.

questions.name: Associated Publications
questions.description: Presence of formal citations or external resources with DOI-linked references.
questions.score_label: Two or more distinct references plus a formal dataset citation
questions.evidence: citation: a formal dataset citation naming authors ('Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., ... Ghosh, S.'), year (2026), title 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information', version 3.1.0, publisher PhysioNet, RRID:SCR_007345 and https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66. Distinct additional references: (1) the Interspeech 2024 protocol development paper, Bensoussan et al., 'Developing Multi-Disorder Voice Protocols', Proc. Interspeech 2024, 1445-1449, with an ISCA archive URL and, via related_datasets is_documented_by, DOI 10.21437/Interspeech.2024-1926; (2) the REDCap data dictionary archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724; (3) the documentation repository archived at https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653; (4) the b2aiprep and SenseLab repositories; (5) Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles.
questions.quality_note: Both conditions for 5 are met and neither marginally: a formal citation identifying the dataset by title, authors, version and publisher, plus at least five distinct further references of which three carry DOIs. Scored on the permitted values 0, 3 or 5.
questions.semantic_analysis: Counted distinct resources rather than links, so the repeated b2aiprep URL (external_resources and extension_mechanism.contribution_url) and the Interspeech paper appearing in both external_resources and related_datasets were each counted once. The citation's author order matches the creators list and its senior author matches Satrajit Ghosh's stated role as 'senior author of the version 3.1.0 release'. The DOI in the citation matches the record's doi field exactly, and 10.21437 is ISCA's correct registrant prefix.

questions.name: Human Subject Representation
questions.applicability_evidence: Established on the same non-Q15 evidence as Q8: description names '833 adult participants recruited at five North American sites' selected for voice, neurological, mood/psychiatric and respiratory conditions plus controls (Q1/Q2); keywords include 'health' (Q3); collection_mechanisms and data_collectors describe in-clinic collection with a trained research assistant (Q12).
questions.description: Inclusion of human subjects, demographic diversity, or subgroup details.
questions.score_label: Subgroups characterized with partial demographic and eligibility detail
questions.evidence: instances: 833 human participants with a label_description explaining clinician-assigned diagnosis and, for the psychiatric cohort, EHR or active prescription. subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present true; identification lists age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status plus assignment to voice, neurological/neurodegenerative, mood/psychiatric or respiratory cohorts or controls; distribution states that releases 'do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories' and that the dataset 'has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors'. at_risk_populations: adults only, minimum age 18 and maximum 120, pediatric participants released separately, assent options, discomfort risk in mood cohorts. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling. Eligibility fragments: known_limitations records that 'eligibility required the ability to read and speak English'; sampling_strategies refers to 'per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria' without enumerating them. The phenotype collection names eighteen diagnosis files and thirteen questionnaire instruments (GAD-7, PHQ-9, VHI-10, PTSD adult, dyspnea index, Leicester cough questionnaire and others).
questions.quality_note: Well above general human-subject description: cohorts, demographic variable categories, age bounds, language eligibility, per-condition phenotype files and a stated distributional skew. Held at 4 because no demographic distributions are reported — no counts or proportions by sex, race, ethnicity, age band or cohort — and the per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria are referred to but never listed, so a user cannot assess representativeness quantitatively before requesting access.
questions.semantic_analysis: The demographic categories named here are consistent with the identifiers_removed list, which withholds state and province and 'select geographic or demographic identifiers' — so some of the absent granularity is a deliberate privacy choice rather than a documentation lapse, and that mitigates but does not remove the gap, since aggregate counts would not breach Safe Harbor. Population claims are consistent across fields: adult-only enrollment in at_risk_populations matches the description's '833 adult participants' and the separate pediatric release recorded in related_datasets as 10.13026/h995-bt35 covering ages 2 to 18.

questions.name: Findability (Persistent Links)
questions.description: Dataset includes persistent URLs for access and documentation.
questions.score_label: Pass — persistent identifiers and working external links present
questions.evidence: page: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; distribution_formats[*].access_urls repeat the PhysioNet landing page; external_resources supply https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, https://github.com/sensein/senselab, https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.12760724, https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.13834653, https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/ and an ISCA archive URL; raw audio at https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/.
questions.quality_note: Passes decisively: a version-pinned landing page, a DOI, prior-version DOIs and numerous documentation and code locators.
questions.semantic_analysis: All URLs are structurally well-formed and their domains match the roles claimed (physionet.org for the release, synapse.org for controlled-access audio, zenodo.org for archival snapshots, github.com for code). The DOI-to-landing-page relationship required by FAIR logic holds: the 10.13026 prefix resolves to the publisher named in the record.

questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on non-Q17 fields: third_party_sharing.is_shared is true and describes distribution 'through a data publishing platform that provides publicly accessible metadata and a DOI', and file_collections enumerate the released files (Q4).
questions.description: Describes how users can obtain the dataset (download, DUA, login).
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path with explicit access tier
questions.evidence: Tier for features: 'users register on PhysioNet, confirm their identity under the Registered Access License, and sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement; from version 3.0.0 the applicant must be a credentialed PhysioNet user', with 'no additional training is required' and 'no fees associated with these restrictions'. Tier for raw audio: 'a Data Access Request Form, a Data Use Agreement, review by the Data Access Compliance Office and a Data Use and Transfer Agreement signed by an authorized official at the recipient institution', served through Synapse, requests to DACO@b2ai-voice.org, with the agreement effective 'only upon review and approval by the Data Access Compliance Office'. distribution_formats give formats with access_urls to the version-pinned landing page. third_party_sharing describes independent application by collaborating institutions.
questions.quality_note: Meets the top band. Both access tiers are named, the required artifacts and approving body are identified for each, the credentialing requirement is version-scoped, costs are stated, and a contact address is given. A user knows exactly what to do and what they will and will not receive.
questions.semantic_analysis: The access description is consistent with the licence and with confidentiality_level 'restricted', and the record avoids the common error of calling a DUA-gated release 'public' — it states plainly that the platform provides 'publicly accessible metadata and a DOI while the dataset itself requires registered or credentialed access'. There is no download_url field, but access_urls inside distribution_formats discharge the same function; scoring treated the landing page plus the documented credentialing path as a complete access route.

questions.name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
questions.description: License clearly defined with explicit use guidance including intended, prohibited and discouraged uses, and social impact analysis with mitigation strategies.
questions.score_label: License + comprehensive use guidance + social impact analysis with mitigation
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms as above, with data_use_permission: general_research_use. intended_uses: two entries with use_category research, usage_notes and examples ('AI model pretraining', 'fine-tuning', 'benchmarking', 'validation'), the second restating the agreement's scope for Authorized Researchers. prohibited_uses: three entries each with a reason — re-identification attempts and actions that could reasonably lead to re-identification; uses that could foreseeably cause harm or stigmatization to participants, families, communities or populations; IP-based restriction of access to the data or to conclusions derived from it. discouraged_uses: non-clinical and non-research applications including hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustment and surveillance, with the rationale that these 'could negatively impact individuals based on their health conditions or voice characteristics'. future_use_impacts: two entries covering distributional skew ('unexamined use could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups', with the mitigation that users should consider the multivariate distribution) and discriminatory deployment (mitigated by exclusion under the access agreement). Supported by known_limitations (five typed entries with scope_impact and recommended_mitigation), content_warnings and existing_uses.
questions.quality_note: Top band on every component. Notably, the prohibitions are tied to reasons rather than asserted, and each social-impact risk is paired with a concrete mitigation — one behavioural (assess the multivariate distribution) and one contractual (excluded by the access agreement).
questions.semantic_analysis: Use guidance is coherent with governance: the re-identification prohibition matches participant_privacy's contractual bar on contacting subjects, the anti-IP-restriction prohibition matches ip_restrictions clause two, and the discouraged surveillance and insurance uses match the future_use_impacts risk narrative. The licence is restrictive while the IP terms are deliberately open (Fort Lauderdale Agreement, no obstruction of downstream research), which is internally consistent rather than contradictory: access is gated for participant protection, not to enclose the science.

questions.name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
questions.description: Presence of version access, errata, update plans, source derivation, parent dataset linkages, missing data documentation, data split indicators, and provenance graph representation.
questions.score_label: Complete lineage in text form: entities, activities, agents and derivation paths
questions.evidence: was_derived_from: 'Raw audio recordings of standardized acoustic tasks captured by the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application, together with questionnaire and clinical data captured in REDCap, collected under the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol.' raw_data_sources: two source entities with format (WAV audio; REDCap export) and access_details, the audio identified by Synapse accession syn72370534. related_datasets: derives_from syn72370534 and is_new_version_of 10.13026/k81f-qr68. Activities and agents: preprocessing_strategies name each transformation with parameters, machine_annotation_tools attribute each transformation to a named tool, b2aiprep version 3.0.0 is identified as the library that 'generated this release', and data_collectors and creators identify the human agents. version_access, errata and updates as under Q13. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling strategy with a released missingness table. splits: no predefined splits, with users encouraged to construct their own. Quality artifacts: audio_quality_metrics.tsv released per recording, and an audit protocol under cleaning_strategies. parent_datasets: absent.
questions.quality_note: The lineage is complete and traversable in text form, which the rubric accepts as equivalent to a graph when it supplies full lineage: for any released file a reader can name the source entity, the transforming activity with its parameters, the software agent that performed it and the release in which it changed. Integrity and quality are supported by per-recording QC metrics and a documented audit, and errata record concrete corrections including the 3.1.0 Parquet repair and diagnosis back-fill.
questions.semantic_analysis: Derivation paths resolve per file rather than in aggregate — sparc_ema.parquet traces to the SPARC package and to the 16 kHz standardized waveform, ppgs.parquet to the ppgs package at 100 Hz, static_features.tsv to openSMILE/Praat/parselmouth — so entity-activity-agent relationships are recoverable without a formal PROV-O serialization. parent_datasets is empty, but the derives_from relationship carries the same information with a typed relation and a resolvable accession, so the absence does not break the chain. One residual limitation: the raw-audio entity is identified by Synapse accession only, since no DOI exists for it, which the record states explicitly.

questions.name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
questions.description: Metadata documents known biases using standardized taxonomies aligned with CROISSANT RAI standards, and includes fairness analysis.
questions.score_label: Taxonomy-categorized biases with mitigations; fairness analysis qualitative only
questions.evidence: known_biases: three entries using BiasTypeEnum values. selection_bias — recruitment at 'a small number of high volume expert clinics', with groups having 'less trust in the medical system or in AI, or who are less proximal to the collection sites' less likely to be recruited; mitigation_strategy of shifting toward remote collection and controlling more recruitment variables. representation_bias — skews by disorder category, site and demographics, unequal disease distribution across releases; mitigation that users should consider the multivariate distribution. measurement_bias — participants screened for different disorders by site, so 'participants with different labels also had their data collected on different devices, confounding label with recording apparatus and site', with affected_subsets naming all disease cohorts. future_use_impacts: distributional skew and unexamined use 'could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups'; discriminatory deployment outside research. Supporting: anomalies (site configuration differences, protocol change over the study, noise artifacts, variable diagnostic practice, headset distance variation) and known_limitations (representativeness, English-only coverage, temporal shift in diagnostic criteria).
questions.quality_note: Above the basic-identification band: biases are typed with standard enum values, each is explained mechanistically, two carry mitigation strategies and one names affected subsets. Held at 4 because fairness analysis remains qualitative — no subgroup performance or distributional analysis, no quantified skew, and no mapping to AI Ontology (AIO) terms — so a user is told a skew exists but not its magnitude along any demographic axis.
questions.semantic_analysis: The bias taxonomy is used correctly rather than decoratively: the measurement_bias entry identifies a genuine label-apparatus confound that follows from the per-site iPad assignment recorded in collection_mechanisms, meaning the bias documentation is corroborated by the collection documentation. This is the strongest form of bias reporting in the record. The gap is the same one flagged at Q15 — no demographic distributions are given — which makes the representation_bias claim unquantifiable and leaves a modeler unable to weight or stratify without first obtaining the data.

strengths: Ethics and privacy documentation is exceptionally complete and, more importantly, substantively matched to the data: Safe Harbor for tabular phenotypes is paired with total withholding of raw waveforms precisely because voice is itself a biometric identifier, and free-speech-derived spectrograms are excluded rather than merely warned about.

Governance is decomposed into an accountable institution (USF Board of Trustees), a reviewing committee (DACO), five named stewardship roles, two distinct access tiers with their required artifacts, and a working contact address — a reader can execute the access path without further inquiry.

Preprocessing is documented at parameter level (25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 Mel bins, sparc at 50 Hz, ppgs at 100 Hz over 40 phonemes) and every tool maps onto specific released files, making the feature tables reproducible from raw audio.

Provenance forms a complete textual lineage — source entities with accessions, parameterized activities, named software agents with a version for the generating library, and per-version errata — satisfying the rubric's full-lineage criterion without a formal PROV-O serialization.

Bias documentation uses BiasTypeEnum correctly and identifies a real, mechanistically explained label-apparatus confound arising from per-site device assignment, corroborated by the collection description elsewhere in the record.

The record marks source conflicts explicitly with source_caveats (author spellings, grant identifier variants, healthsheet answers written against earlier releases, BIDS conformance not asserted for this layout) instead of silently choosing, which materially raises confidence in its unqualified statements.
weaknesses: version_access.latest_version_doi (10.13026/37yb-1t42) matches no version the record enumerates and is not the dataset's own DOI, leaving the pointer to the latest release unresolvable — the one uncaveated identifier inconsistency in an otherwise carefully caveated document.

No demographic distributions are reported: subpopulations names the variables collected and states that skews exist, but gives no counts or proportions by sex, race, ethnicity, age band or cohort, so the representation_bias claim cannot be quantified and representativeness cannot be assessed before requesting access.

keywords carries only four generic terms and does not reflect the eighteen diagnostic categories enumerated elsewhere, so condition-driven discovery depends on prose inside a file_collections description.

No data-level standard is asserted for this release (conforms_to absent; BIDS conformance documented only for a different layout), and no byte sizes or total file count are given, limiting harmonization and download planning.

hipaa_compliant: compliant is left in unreconciled tension with the DTUA's own statement that the transferred data is 'not covered under HIPAA, FERPA, or similar laws', and no data protection impact analysis exists for a dataset carrying race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, psychiatric diagnoses and biometric voice.

collection_timeframes gives a 12-month duration with no calendar bounds, drawn from documentation written against an earlier release, which is difficult to reconcile with six releases spanning November 2024 to May 2026.
recommendations: Resolve version_access.latest_version_doi: either identify 10.13026/37yb-1t42 as the version-independent PhysioNet project DOI in version_details, or point it at doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66.

Add aggregate demographic counts to subpopulations (participants by sex, age band, race/ethnicity and cohort, and by site where disclosure permits), which quantifies the declared skew without breaching Safe Harbor.
Enumerate the per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria referenced in sampling_strategies, alongside the already-stated age bounds and English-language eligibility.
Extend keywords with condition, modality and population terms bound where possible to the ICD-10 codes already named as the annotation protocol.
State calendar start and end dates for the collection behind version 3.1.0, or record that collection is ongoing and scope the 12-month figure to the initial accrual period.

Scope the HIPAA statement to the released registered-access feature set and note separately that the raw-audio DTUA governs data the provider treats as PII outside HIPAA; record whether the ethics module's sensitive-field review functions as a DPIA-equivalent assessment.
Record byte sizes per file_collection and a total file count, and state whether the features/metadata/phenotype layout derives from BIDS or follows a nameable sidecar-dictionary convention.

metadata.notes: Single-record evaluation. No other evaluation artifact was read. All twenty questions were scored as applicable: the human-subjects condition (Q8, Q15), the datasets-shared condition (Q10, Q17), the software-output condition (Q11) and the collection-plus-shared condition (Q12, Q13) were each resolved on fields belonging to other questions, per the anti-circular rule.
